title: Death in cells: City police to release autopsy results when investigation wraps
article: It may be weeks before autopsy results for a 54-year-old man who died in Edmonton city police holding cells are made public.

The man was arrested on warrants near 108 Avenue and 101 Street around 9:50 a.m. last Wednesday and, about 10 minutes later, was placed in downtown division cells at headquarters, police said Thursday.

When the man was found unresponsive in the cell just before noon, the paramedic on duty, along with other staff on hand, administered first-aid until emergency medical services (EMS) arrived. EMS continued to treat him on scene but he died.
Alberta's director of law enforcement was notified of the death and ordered the case to remain in the hands of Edmonton city police, rather than the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT).
The city police homicide unit is leading the investigation and although an autopsy was done Thursday, results will not be made known until the case is concluded, police said.
Edmonton's last in-custody death was in November when a 28-year-old man died and ASIRT was ordered to investigate.

On Nov. 14 at about 8 a.m., Edmonton city police responded to the University of Alberta to help peace officers from the campus with a man who had been trespassing inside the Students' Union Building, 8900 114 St. Police said he appeared to be extremely intoxicated, had difficulty standing and was found to be in violation of his bail conditions and probation order so he was arrested.

Officers noted the man was shaking and unable to sit still and could not walk without help. Shortly after 9 a.m. at southwest division, police had the man medically assessed and he was cleared for custody.

Once transported to the detainee management unit at 2 p.m., the man was medically assessed again and cleared for custody. However, when transported to the Edmonton Remand Centre, a third medical assessment raised concerns and the man was taken to hospital. The man's condition continued to deteriorate and, on Nov. 16, he died in hospital.
ASIRT investigators met with family members prior to the man's death.

As the man's condition deteriorated while in custody, Edmonton police provided notification under the Police Act and ASIRT was directed to investigate. It is not yet known whether the man's worsening condition was because of a medical event or injury. The investigation is focused on whether police conduct caused or contributed to the man's condition and death, said ASIRT.
